title: A clearer tomorrow.
subtitle: Stockwise · Demand and inventory planning
text: For a small business, tomorrow starts with a question: what should I buy today? Too little stock means missed sales. Too much means waste and cash sitting on a shelf. Meet Stockwise, a planning copilot for everyday business decisions.

title: One daily workspace.
subtitle: Synthetic restaurant data · Working local prototype
text: Here is Saffron Kitchen, our synthetic restaurant workspace. The dashboard brings together tomorrow's expected servings, a purchase estimate, items to replenish, and measured forecast error. The daily brief points the owner toward the decisions that need attention. These are demonstration records, and we are not claiming measured savings at a real business.

title: Forecasts with evidence.
subtitle: 7–14 days · Time-ordered holdout · Transparent baseline
text: The forecast explorer shows each dish over seven or fourteen days. We start with an understandable same-weekday baseline and exclude unavailable observations from training. A rolling-origin backtest compares it with a moving average using only earlier data. The displayed ranges are heuristic, not calibrated guarantees. The point is to show evidence and limitations alongside the numbers.

title: From plates to ingredients.
subtitle: Approved recipes · Shared ingredients · Preparation yields
text: Restaurants need ingredients, not just dish forecasts. Stockwise expands approved recipes and aggregates shared ingredients across dishes. Grams become kilograms, and prepared vegetable weights account for trimming yield. Purchased weights are not adjusted twice. Stock lots retain expiry dates, and confirmed receipts retain arrival dates, so unusable stock and late deliveries cannot hide a shortage.

title: A purchase draft you can inspect.
subtitle: Need + safety − allocated stock − timely receipts
text: The purchase planner makes the arithmetic visible. Required ingredients plus the chosen safety allowance, minus allocated stock and timely receipts, produce a shortfall. That shortfall rounds up to supplier packs and minimum orders. Each supplier's lead time and review period define the purchase coverage. The owner can see excess caused by rounding and review delivery risk. No order is placed automatically.

title: What if tomorrow is busier?
subtitle: Explicit +25% scenario · Recalculated forecast and purchases
text: Now we increase expected demand by twenty-five percent. The same planning tools recalculate ingredient needs and purchase quantities. This is an explicit owner assumption, not a claimed causal promotion model. Stock counts can also be updated, and the local audit log records changes.

title: Meta explains the planning numbers.
subtitle: Live Muse Spark 1.3 · Inspectable recipe and purchase tool results
text: Now we ask the copilot how much rice to purchase. Meta's Muse Spark selects the purchase and recipe tools, reads the real planning outputs, and explains the shortfall and pack rounding. This is a verified live model response. The interface shows the returned model, latency, token use, and tool evidence. If the API is unavailable, the numerical planner still works with a clearly labeled local fallback.

title: A little foresight goes a long way.
subtitle: Restaurant + retail · CSV import and export · Local prototype
text: The same engine also supports retail products. Owners can import validated daily sales and export purchase drafts. Stockwise turns business records into a practical next action: know what will sell, calculate what you need, and buy with a little foresight.
